title: Juicy Molten Russian Rest-Meat Pancakes
description: A rich, savory pancake dish featuring a molten center, crumbled rest-meat, and tangy pickles. This low-carb friendly recipe showcases the bold flavors of Russia.
instructions: Preheat a tava-griddle or non-stick skillet over medium heat. In a large bowl, combine ground rest-meat, cottage cheese, sour cream, pickled cucumbers, chopped fresh dill, salt, and black pepper. Mix well to combine.
Add egg yolks, melted butter, heavy cream, shredded cheddar cheese, and dried oregano to the bowl. Stir until smooth batter forms.
Using a 1/4 cup measuring cup, scoop the batter onto the preheated tava-griddle. Cook for 2-3 minutes, until the edges start to set.
Flip the pancakes and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, until the centers are still slightly molten.
Serve immediately, garnished with additional chopped fresh dill if desired.
Repeat with the remaining batter, until all the pancakes are cooked. Serve hot, with your choice of toppings.
Note: Traditionally, these pancakes would be cooked in a cast-iron skillet over an open flame, allowing the center to stay molten.
To make ahead, cook the pancakes and store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat before serving.
To freeze, place cooked pancakes on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, and freeze until solid. Transfer to a freezer-safe bag or container for up to 3 months.
To reheat, wrap the frozen pancakes in a damp paper towel and microwave for 20-30 seconds, or until warmed through.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
